question: Two nuclei have mass numbers $27$ and $216$. Compare their radii using $R = R_{0}A^{1/3}$. Also explain why the heavier nucleus has more nucleons.

options.A: Since $R\propto A$, the radius ratio is $27:216=1:8$. The heavier nucleus has more nucleons because it has a larger radius.
options.B: Using $R\propto A^{1/3}$, $R_1:R_2=3:6=1:3$. The heavier nucleus has more nucleons because all nuclei have equal mass numbers.
options.C:
Using $R\propto A^{1/3}$, $R_1:R_2=27^{1/3}:216^{1/3}=3:6=1:2$.
Mass number represents total nucleons, so the nucleus with $A=216$ has more nucleons than the one with $A=27$.
options.D: The radii are equal because nuclear radius does not depend on mass number; both nuclei have the same number of nucleons.
